speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin, could you describe the specific nature of your gait and limb ataxia, and when did these symptoms first appear?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any headaches, vision changes, or difficulty swallowing recently? Also, do you have a history of alcohol use or any previous neurological conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and natalizumab use, I am concerned about Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML), so I will order an MRI of the brain to look for characteristic lesions. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI confirms Progressive Multifocal Leucoencephalopathy (PML), a serious opportunistic infection associated with natalizumab therapy. DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
